quotes.text: A firewall mostly watches where traffic is going. While this one reads what the traffic says. That difference is the whole reason it exists, and it's where almost every beginner gets it wrong.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures in one contrast what makes a web application firewall different from a network firewall.

quotes.text: Detection mode exists, so you can be wrong about your rules in private before your own users feel it.

quotes.text: You might think of Azure WAF as the shield over your whole Microsoft world, but it's actually the lock on the one door you built yourself.

quotes.why: Clears up the common misconception that Azure WAF protects the Microsoft 365 tenant.

takeaways: Azure Web Application Firewall reads what web requests say and blocks known attack patterns such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting, based on OWASP-derived managed rule sets.
It runs as a policy on Application Gateway for regional apps or Front Door for global apps, and should be tuned in detection mode before switching production to prevention mode.
It is not DDoS protection, cannot fix broken access control, needs a locked-down origin, and does not protect your Microsoft 365 tenant, only the apps you host yourself.
hook: Many people assume a firewall is a firewall, but a web application firewall reads what traffic says rather than where it goes. This Simply Explained episode is for beginners and Azure admins who want to know what Azure Web Application Firewall catches, where it lives, how its scoring and modes work, what it costs and what it cannot protect.
